text:
Colorado had the puck most of the night in Denver. The Avalanche attempted 77 shots to Nashville's 51. The Predators blocked 25 of them, Justus Annunen stopped 30 of the 32 that reached him, and Steven Stamkos ended it 2:18 into overtime with a power-play slap shot.

Annunen is the story under the story. The Avalanche drafted him 64th overall in 2018, and on Thursday he saved 1.2 goals more than his shots deserved against them. His biggest stop came in overtime, on a Devon Toews chance worth 0.26 expected goals (expected goals measure how often a shot like that goes in), with the game on the line. By our count he added 0.54 wins, the most of anyone in the building, a hair ahead of Stamkos.

The goals came in a back-and-forth first 25 minutes. Ross Colton opened the scoring at 4:01 with Ryan O'Reilly assisting. Jaden Schwartz tied it at 9:11. Then Vitali Pinchuk, who never got drafted and spent last season scoring 66 points for Dinamo Minsk in the KHL, scored his first NHL goal at 14:34, a backhand our numbers gave a 4% chance. Parker Kelly tied it again at 5:08 of the second, and nobody scored for the rest of regulation. Mackenzie Blackwood was good at the other end too, half a goal better than expected.

Volume flattered Colorado. Nashville actually created more by quality, 3.53 expected goals to 3.19, and won 56% of our replays of the game's shots. A lot of the Predators' edge came on the power play (1 for 5, 1.37 expected goals), including the one that mattered: Stamkos from Roman Josi and O'Reilly, a goal that took Nashville's win chance from 48% to 100%. O'Reilly had two assists in 24 and a half minutes.

That is three straight wins for the Predators, and two wins over Colorado already, after a 6-2 game on Oct. 25. The Avalanche will look at T.J. Hughes's 30% chance that Annunen stopped in the first period and wonder how a game this lopsided in attempts got away from them. It got away because the shots that mattered were Nashville's.
headline: Stamkos ends it, and Annunen beats his old team
